note: The seven letters A to G (note-names:1): said up the white keys of a piano, up and down a staff that starts on A, then guessed one step above and below and checked by tapping. Each section has one feel to reach or one thing to do when it goes wrong. Staff and piano-keys can't be told to label by letter ("labels" takes degree or solfege), so the letters show while the player's label setting is note names, the default.

exercise.title: The seven letters, A to G
exercise.why: Music names its notes with seven letters, A to G, and then starts again at A, so once you can say them up and down from any letter you can name every white key.

cells.text:
The piano below marks its white keys with their letters. Tap the white keys from one {{c}} up to the next, and say each letter as you tap. After {{g}} the letters start again at {{a}}.
Practice until you say the letters without reading them.

The staff below shows the same seven letters starting on {{a}}: tap a note to hear it. Tap up the staff from the lowest note and say each letter, then come back down.
Practice until the letters come as easily on the way down as on the way up.

This staff starts on {{c}}. Pick any note and say the letter of the note above it, then tap that note and read its label to check.
Then guess the note below each time, which is the harder way round.
